resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. slides §1 line 74: scope: The finding rests on a false factual premise. The judge says `[Lecture: What packaging is]` (line 57) is "a bare link title carrying no content into this deck." That is wrong. A standalone-paragraph include-link is how a file gets inlined. `scripts/build-workbook.js` `inlineIncludes()` (line 310ff) replaces it with the lecture's full body inside a `.phase--lecture` wrapper, and `site/layouts/slides.js` `buildDeckModel` puts those phases into the composed module deck. check_slides.md §13 says the same thing: "Structural include-links (standalone-paragraph `[Title](exercises/<slug>.md)`) ... are how the file gets inlined."

So in the composed deck, the what-packaging-is slides come before `## Inspect your results` (include at L57, section at L70). The lecture's slide `## The optimum is local, and it moves` (curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md L59–61) introduces "the kit" and glosses it right away through contrast: "the same task without the kit, then with it. The un-packaged send-off is the baseline; the packaged experiment testing the kit is running right now." It then says "Where the two sessions disagree, you'll know ... which failure the kit catches here, and which still recurs." Module L74 is a near-verbatim callback to that slide, not a cold referent.

§1 at current wording (rule.js slides 1) lists "a term introduced on an earlier slide ... reused" as NOT a violation. Its module-arc carve-out also says "Module include-order = deck order more generally", and says content a lecture earlier in the same module's include order taught counts as prior context. The judge treated the arc-earned-vocabulary carve-out as the only possible exemption and missed the include-order clause. The "never named" failure class does not apply: the term appears earlier in the composed deck, glossed in the same sentence where it is introduced.

In the long-read layout the same inlining applies, so the lecture text also comes before L74 there. The fix is not needed, and applying it would break a deliberate echo of the lecture's wording. / harm: The finding depends on a false fact. The judge says `[Lecture: What packaging is]` (line 57) is "a bare link title carrying no content into this deck". It isn't. `scripts/build-workbook.js` `inlineIncludes()` (around L313) replaces every standalone-paragraph include link with the included file's full body, and `postProcessIncludes()` wraps that body in `<section class="phase phase--lecture">`. Under check_slides §10, that wrapper is exactly what reaches the composed deck. So in the module deck, all of `curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md` sits in order before `## Inspect your results`, followed by the-gate-is-a-claim.

That lecture's slide `## The optimum is local, and it moves` uses "the kit" three times (what-packaging-is.md L59, L61), and its wording matches line 74 almost word for word: "Where the two sessions disagree, you'll know something ...: which failure the kit catches here, and which still recurs." Line 74 is a deliberate callback to a slide the reader saw a few slides earlier in the same deck.

§1 also covers this case directly. Its module-arc carve-out says "Module include-order = deck order more generally" and counts content taught by an immediately-preceding lecture in the module's include order as prior context. So "the kit" is not "never named". It is a term introduced on an earlier slide of the composed deck and reused, which is the rule's own example of a non-violation.

The no-M6 flag makes no difference. The `<!--flag:no-module:spot-gaps-build-the-loop-->` block only controls whether `## Inspect your results` renders. The lecture include at line 57 is outside the flag and is inlined in both variants.

Harm lens:
- (a) No one in the room hits a cold referent.
- (b) The claimed harm is only the rule restated, on a false premise.
- (c) The proposed swap to "the packaging" would break the echo of the lecture sentence and the "credit the kit" callback on line 75.
- (d) The meaning is already carried by the lecture slides just before this one.
